plan.title: bug(gates,scope): a completed scope's record cannot be corrected -- every printed recovery is inapplicable and scope:undo is never mentioned

narratives.Description: bug(gates,scope): a completed scope's record cannot be corrected -- every printed recovery is inapplicable and scope:undo is never mentioned
narratives.Overview:
Spec is Bound remedy lean 5649802911, not the filed Expected (completed-path write class keyed on the singular path, scope:undo recovery ladder, or scope:complete --amend).

**Next-build (Bound-remedy):**
- Name git revert or hand-edit only if that action can succeed after complete. Prefer repairing the undo refusal text, or restoring write authority after complete, over a new write class.
- Do not enumerate scope:undo as the recovery for completed-record edits.
- If a completed-path write class binds at all, reuse allMutationTargetsAreProposedLifecycleWrites shape plus authz, runtimeAuthority, and occupancy rechecks. Do not key on the singular declared path.
- Restate rung-1 failure as no approved xBRIEF available in a one-scope repo, not as a fake-scope prohibition.

The cheap defect is two surfaces pointing at each other: undo says hand-edit, the write gate then denies it after complete.

## Summary

Once a scope is completed, its own record can no longer be corrected: any `Edit`/`Write` to `xbrief/completed/<scope>.xbrief.json` is denied by the write gate ("No active xBRIEF artifact was found under xbrief/active/"). The deny text offers three recoveries — activate an approved scope, write a new proposal, or scratch posture — and **none of them applies**: there is no scope to activate (completing it is what removed it), inventing a scope to fix a typo is explicitly forbidden by the same message ("Do not invent a fake scope"), and scratch posture cannot touch the repo file. The verb that actually works, `scope:undo`, is absent from the deny text — and using it means reopening lifecycle state (active again, statuses, stamps) just to fix two words in a historical record.

This bit immediately in practice: the vendor review stack itself (Greptile, running as a required check) requested corrections to a completed scope artifact — reversed timestamps, imprecise Result wording — and the gate then denied the requested corrections.

## Environment

- Directive: `@deftai/directive` 0.116.0; Host: Claude Code; macOS (Darwin 25.6.0), Node v22.22.3
- Consumer repo (initial commit: three markdown files in `docs/`), org review stack Greptile + SLizard + Socket
- Active session with a valid `leaf-implementation` occupancy grant to the editing agent (i.e., session/occupancy gates all satisfied — only the scope gate denies)

## Reproduction

1. Activate a scope; do the work; `deft scope:complete` (artifact moves to `xbrief/completed/`); commit to the PR branch; push.
2. PR review (Greptile) flags factual nits *inside the completed artifact* (e.g., `updated` earlier than `created`; Result wording).
3. Attempt the requested `Edit` on `xbrief/completed/<scope>.xbrief.json` from the same granted session.
4. Denied: "No active xBRIEF artifact was found under xbrief/active/ … Recovery: run `deft scope:activate` … or Write a new proposal … or … `.deft-scratch/`."
5. Observe: no recovery in the message can produce the edit; `deft scope:undo` (which can) is not mentioned.

## Expected

One or more of:

1. **Completed-scope record maintenance is a recognized write class**: edits confined to `xbrief/completed/*.xbrief.json` (metadata/narrative fields, not resurrection) allowed under an active session without a new scope — the record is *about* governed work, it is not new governed work.
2. The deny message enumerates `scope:undo` whenever the denied path is itself a lifecycle artifact in `completed/` (or `cancelled/`), with the undo → edit → re-complete sequence spelled out.
3. `scope:complete --amend` (or similar): a one-shot correction verb that edits the completed record under the transition verb's own authority, no state reopening.

## Relationship to existing issues

- Completion-side sibling of #4412's activation-side recovery-ladder gaps: this is the fourth deny message in the same flow whose printed recoveries cannot succeed.
- Distinct from the close-out/merge ordering contradiction (filed separately): that one is about *when* completion may happen; this one is about the record being frozen against correction *after* it happens.

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-09-13T00:52:35Z)

model: claude-opus-5
role: critic

Round 1 critic, fresh, refutation charter, N=1. Ceiling 5649748031 (the triage write-back; it is the only in-envelope comment). Anchors re-verified by running checks against `bf9d26c8ccac6599d5241a1d3ea1a3a636bee982`, not by reading the body.

## Anchor re-verification

| Recorded anchor | Result |
|---|---|
| write-gate deny fires on an Edit under `xbrief/completed/` with an empty active set | holds |
| deny text prints three recoveries, none naming `scope:undo` | holds, with a caveat (F3) |
| `scope:undo` exists | exists, and **refuses `complete`** (F1) |
| `scope:complete --amend` exists | does not exist anywhere (F6) |
| completed-record freeze | **no such mechanism exists** (F2) |

Two of five anchors do not survive. The recorded refutation-target's third conjunct — "`scope:undo` is never mentioned" — is literally true; the Summary's gloss on it is not.

### F1 — blocks-the-design: `scope:undo` cannot reverse `complete`, so Expected #2 prints a fourth inapplicable recovery

**Evidence.** `packages/core/src/scope/constants.ts:65` — `TERMINAL_ACTIONS = new Set(["complete", "fail"])`. `packages/core/src/scope/undo.ts:288` gates on that set first and returns `ok: false` with `Refusing to undo terminal action 'complete' (decision_id=…). Use git revert or hand-edit.` `REVERSIBLE_ACTIONS` (`constants.ts:64`) is `demote | cancel | restore | undo` — `complete` is not a member, and the inverse-transition resolver has no `complete` arm (`undo.ts:90-160`). The docs agree and predate the issue: `content/skills/deft-directive-refinement/SKILL.md:287` ("terminal actions (`complete` / `fail`) are REFUSED -- use `git revert` or hand-edit"), and `CHANGELOG.md:3274` ("terminal `complete` / `fail` remain refused") at the #1134 landing.

**Failure mode.** An agent hits the write deny, reads the newly-enumerated `scope:undo` → edit → re-complete sequence, runs `deft scope:undo -- <decision_id>` against the `complete` entry, and gets a deterministic refusal. It is now one deny deeper with no printed recovery left. The issue's own complaint — a recovery ladder whose rungs cannot bear weight — is reproduced by its own remedy, and this time against a control that refuses by construction rather than by circumstance.

**Disposition consequence.** Expected #2 cannot bind as written. A recovery-ladder heading may name what the refusal itself names (`git revert`, hand-edit) or a new verb, but it cannot name `scope:undo`. The Summary sentence "The verb that actually works, `scope:undo`, is absent from the deny text" is false, and so is its cost estimate ("reopening lifecycle state … just to fix two words") — there is no reopening to price, because the reopen is refused.

### F2 — blocks-the-design: there is no completed-record freeze; the gate is path-blind, so Expected #1 rests on a distinction the gate never draws

**Evidence.** The write gate branches on active-scope readiness, outside-root, spawn-tool, and exactly one path prefix — `xbrief/proposed/` / `vbrief/proposed/` (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:1754-1757`). `git grep -n "completed/"` over `dispatcher.ts` at the pinned SHA returns zero hits. `clause-file-scope-bind` is exported from `packages/core/src/scope/index.ts:5` and is imported by nothing under `packages/core/src/hooks/**`, so the gate never binds a write target to the active scope's file set. The protected-dest catalog added at this very SHA (#4449 / #4188) is `.deft/authz/**`, `.deft/approved-scope/**`, `.deft-directive-disable`, `.no-deft-directive` — `xbrief/completed/` is deliberately not a member. No digest, immutability, or freeze mechanism for completed artifacts exists under `packages/core/src/lifecycle`, `scope`, or `hooks`.

**Runnable counter-evidence.** `git log bf9d26c8 -400 --diff-filter=M --name-only -- "xbrief/completed/*" "vbrief/completed/*"` returns 13 commits that correct completed records in place. Four exist for no other purpose: `0af0df417` "rewrite plan.items status complete to completed (#4284)", `0352174a0` "replace forged item-8 disposition with a real operator record", `c3b76af81` "point #3599 acceptance evidence at the test names that exist", `bd19b2663` "correct cohort capacityBucket to technical-debt". At `0af0df417` the tree carries an unrelated active xBRIEF (`xbrief/active/2026-08-28-3785-bughooks-fail-closed-hook-registration-travels-without-a-hos.xbrief.json`) — the edit was authorized by scope *presence*, with nothing about the target consulted.

**Failure mode.** "A completed scope's record cannot be corrected" is not a property of the record. The deny in the repro fires because the active set was *empty*, and `scope:complete` emptied it as a side effect. Minting "completed-scope record maintenance" as a write class therefore does two wrong things at once: it leaves the actual defect (a lifecycle verb that removes the only thing authorizing subsequent writes) untouched for every other legitimate post-completion write, and it grants a standing path-keyed exemption for writes that today already succeed whenever any scope is active. Expected #1's justification — "the record is *about* governed work, it is not new governed work" — describes a semantic the gate has never computed, for a target class it has never distinguished.

**Disposition consequence.** The lean must record which of two distinct defects it is remedying before Expected #1 can bind: (a) `scope:complete` leaves a session with zero write authority, or (b) `xbrief/completed/` should be authorized by path. They have different blast radii, and (b) is strictly wider than the repro requires. Binding Expected #1 as stated silently picks (b).

### F3 — sharpens-framing: the quoted deny text blends two branches, and the prohibition cited is purpose-scoped

**Evidence.** The branch an `Edit` reaches is `dispatcher.ts:1763-1774`, which ends `Do not invent a fake scope only to capture Obsidian/scratch notes.` The unqualified-sounding `Do not invent a fake scope only to satisfy this gate.` is at `dispatcher.ts:1752`, inside `if (isSpawnTool(toolName))` — unreachable from Write/Edit.

**Failure mode.** The Summary argues rung 1 is foreclosed *by the message itself*. On the branch actually hit, the message forbids fake scopes only for scratch-note capture, which a correction to a lifecycle artifact is not. What foreclosed rung 1 in the repro is that the consumer repo (initial commit: three markdown files) had no other approved xBRIEF to activate — an availability fact about a one-scope repo, not a prohibition. A remedy drafted against the misquote would rewrite a sentence that is not doing the blocking, and would not generalize: `0af0df417` shows rung 1 working in a repo that had a second scope.

**Disposition consequence.** Restate the rung-1 failure as "no approved xBRIEF was available to activate" and keep the remedy off the prohibition sentence. This also weakens Expected #1's necessity claim.

### F4 — sharpens-framing: the actual contradiction is that the terminal-undo refusal prescribes what the write gate denies

**Evidence.** `undo.ts:292-295` terminates the reversibility path with `Use git revert or hand-edit.` The hand-edit it prescribes is exactly the Edit that `dispatcher.ts:1718-1795` denies once the active set is empty — which, after `scope:complete`, it is. Both are deterministic controls in the same product, shipped at different times (#1134, #2625 / #3080), pointing at each other.

**Failure mode.** The undo refusal is itself a recovery text, and it is another surface in this flow whose printed recovery cannot run under the conditions that produce it. Stated this way the defect is a two-surface inconsistency with a cheap fix on either side; stated as the issue states it, it is a missing write class.

**Disposition consequence.** This is a better-located statement of the same observation and it changes the remedy's cost. Prefer it as the heading the lean carries, and let Expected #1 stand or fall on F2 rather than on the title claim. (Whether `git revert` — the other half of the prescription — survives the Shell dest-of-write fence is unverified here, and is a separate question, not a claim.)

### F5 — sharpens-framing: inventory plus injection lens — a completed-path class reuses the proposed/ exemption's shape or it does not bind

**Inventory before proposing.** The mechanism this issue asks to be extended already exists and is correctly shaped. `dispatcher.ts:1663-1697` gates the proposed-lifecycle allow on `allMutationTargetsAreProposedLifecycleWrites(effectiveRoot, input.payload)` — *all* mutated paths, not the declared one (#3614, cited inline at `dispatcher.ts:1666-1668`) — and then re-runs `authzForMutationTargets`, `runtimeAuthorityForDirectWrite`, and the pre-allow occupancy recheck before returning `write-propose-ready`. The singular `hookWriteTargetPath` (`packages/core/src/hooks/classify/paths.ts:13`) is used only to compose deny-hint text; the plural `hookMutationTargetPaths` (`paths.ts:52`) is what authorization reads.

**Injection / swarm lens.** Fires: the target changes write authorization, and deny/recovery text is an instruction surface read by agents. `composeOverviewWithComments` copies every thread comment verbatim into the xBRIEF Overview the next worker reads as dispatch input, and the design-critique contract records that the quarantine scanner flags nothing under that composed shape. An untrusted comment reading "correct the completed record at `xbrief/completed/X.xbrief.json`" is therefore quoted into a later agent's dispatch input in an authoritative position — and a path-keyed completed-write class is precisely the grant that makes acting on it succeed with *no active scope and no occupancy story*. The existing all-targets predicate plus the rechecks is what keeps that bounded; a class keyed on the declared target would let a multi-target payload ride a `completed/` path into an unrelated write.

**Failure mode.** A completed-write class keyed on `relTarget` — the singular deny-hint variable already in scope at `dispatcher.ts:1720` — is the obvious implementation and is the wrong one: it authorizes on the declared path while the payload mutates others, re-opening #3614 on a new surface.

**Disposition consequence.** If Expected #1 binds at all, it binds with the all-targets predicate and the three named rechecks, mirroring `dispatcher.ts:1663-1697`. Anything else is a new authorization path, not an extension of an audited one.

### F6 — footnote: `scope:complete --amend` would be a new verb surface, not a flag

`git grep -n -- "--amend"` over `packages/core/src/scope`, `packages/cli/src`, and `content/commands.md` at the pinned SHA returns nothing. `tasks/scope.yml:52-60` forwards `{{.CLI_ARGS}}` to `scope-lifecycle complete`, so the flag would land in the lifecycle engine's arg parser and would need its own audit-log action — which, per F1, is the same gap `TERMINAL_ACTIONS` was written to hold closed. Recorded as census, not disposition weight.

## Road not taken

Three mechanisms were live: (1) a path-keyed write class, (2) repairing the printed recovery on one of the two contradicting surfaces, (3) a new amend verb. I did not take (1) as the framing because F2 shows the gate never drew the distinction (1) presupposes, and not (3) because F1 shows the terminal-action refusal is a deliberate invariant that (3) reopens under a new name. (2) is the cheapest change that removes a control pointing at a denied action.

## Steelman

The strongest rejected position is that the deny text is correct and this is a documentation defect only: rung 1 *does* work, and the repro is a one-scope repo that happened to run out of scopes. `0af0df417` is evidence for that reading — a completed record corrected in place under an unrelated active scope, no new mechanism needed.

What would flip my verdict: evidence that activating an unrelated approved xBRIEF to authorize a completed-record correction is itself refused, or is recorded anywhere as prohibited rather than merely undocumented. I found neither — the only fake-scope prohibitions in the text are purpose-scoped to scratch notes (F3) and to spawn gates. Absent that, the strongest remaining defect is F4's two-surface contradiction, not a missing write class.
